title: Paul, again
tomorrow: the Bible's last book has a dragon and plagues. what's the promise?

segments.voice: Acts gave us one word: sent, ordinary people out the door. Today, a letter from one of the travelers, to a church that wasn't getting along.

It turns up at weddings, on greeting cards, on wall art over the couch. In the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Charity is patient, is kind." Here's the odd part. Paul didn't write it for a couple in love. He wrote it to a church in Corinth that was fighting: taking sides over favorite preachers, taking each other to court, showing off their spiritual gifts. So why send a love poem into a feud?
screen: `WEDDINGS, CARDS, WALL ART.` → `CHARITY IS PATIENT, IS KIND.` → `A LOVE POEM INTO A FEUD?`

segments.voice: Because it's medicine, and every line names a symptom. Charity envies not: they were jealous over whose gift looked best. Charity is not puffed up: earlier in the same letter Paul says some of them are puffed up. Charity seeks not her own: at their shared meal, some ate first and others went home hungry. Read that way, the poem is a mirror held up to a quarrel. And look what comes first in the list. Not passion, not romance. Patient. Charity, in the Douay, is the old word for agape in Greek and caritas in Latin, a love that gives. It isn't a donation. It's the love that waits for a slow brother and keeps showing up for a difficult sister. Then Paul's surprise. The Corinthians prized their gifts, prophecy and tongues and knowledge. All of those, he says, will end. Only one thing won't: "Charity never falleth away." Something to tell a friend tonight: that wedding reading was first read out loud to a congregation in the middle of a fight. Which may be the best reason to read it at a wedding.
screen: `EVERY LINE NAMES A SYMPTOM.` · `PATIENT COMES FIRST.` · `AGAPE, CARITAS: A LOVE THAT GIVES.` · `THE GIFTS END; CHARITY DOESN'T.` · then, large: `CHARITY NEVER FALLETH AWAY.`

segments.voice: Read this out loud, slowly, the way you'd say it to someone you're short with lately: charity is patient, is kind. Then say that person's name, and the line once more. Let the sit be patience practice: when you want it to be over, stay.
Paul. The apostle who wrote to a quarreling church that charity is patient and never falls away.
Pocket this one: charity never falleth away, not even in the middle of a feud. See you tomorrow.
